title: Climate Change Adaptation Strategy of the Republic of Croatia to 2040 with a View to 2070
organization: Croatian Parliament; Government of the Republic of Croatia
temporal_coverage: Government strategy adopted in 2020; reports historical sector impacts and RCP4.5 projections for 2011–2040 and 2041–2070, with an outlook to 2070.
methodology: Government strategy blending climate observations, cited damage estimates, projections and sector assessments.
limitations: Historical estimates cite studies; projections use older models and scenario assumptions.

title: Disaster Risk Assessment for the Republic of Croatia
organization: Government of the Republic of Croatia; Directorate of Civil Protection, Ministry of the Interior
temporal_coverage: National disaster-risk assessment dated March 2024; registered county damages cover 2010–2021 and declared natural disasters 2014–2022.
methodology: Government assessment combines hazard scenarios, county vulnerability indicators, recorded losses and civil-protection readiness measures.
limitations: Loss figures aggregate declared disasters and hazards; they do not attribute damages to climate change.

title: Preliminary Flood Risk Assessment 2024
organization: Hrvatske vode (Croatian Waters), national water-management authority
temporal_coverage: The 2024 preliminary assessment uses information through 2023 to identify potentially significant flood-risk areas for the 2028–2033 basin-plan cycle.
methodology: State water authority summarizes mapped potentially significant flood-risk areas and basin population exposure.
limitations: Potential exposure zones are not climate-attributed losses; mapping and management plans are planned for 2028–2033.

title: OECD Economic Surveys: Croatia 2026
organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
temporal_coverage: Economic survey published 30 January 2026; climate event-loss series covers 1980–2023 and includes reported 2024 events and current policy status.
methodology: OECD country survey reviews reported event losses, subnational exposure and adaptation policy.
limitations: The survey cites underlying EEA and EIB material; figures are not independently recalculated here.
